problems.problem: The cobalt ground bar (background.shapes[2], y=1264) floats 25px below the strap's contact shadow (base_y=1239, confirmed present and correctly seated at offset_y=0 in the contact_detail_crop), so the poster carries two disconnected 'grounds': a soft shadow on the paper and a detached printed rule. In a silkscreen concept the rule should BE the ground: move it up to touch the shadow footprint (y=1232) and widen it (x=294, width=492) so it reads as the printed plinth under the 218px contact width instead of a stray line.

The left masthead block (logo y79, title y166-236, subtitle y288-320, rule y377) stops a full 55px above the cobalt bar top (y432) and hugs the top-left corner, leaving a dead cream band between type and geometry; versus reference R1's confident placard stack the block feels under-scaled and untethered. Title size 96 against a 749px hero and 324px decoration rule reads timid; hierarchy logo/title/subtitle is correct but the block needs more presence and a tie into the field.

The red disc (x713,y576,324x346) is clipped by the right canvas edge and sits behind the strap loop with only a thin sliver of overlap, so it reads as a cropped accident rather than a deliberate diagonal anchor; the diagonal cobalt-bar -> hero -> disc announced by the concept is weak because the disc's center of mass falls almost exactly at the hero's vertical middle-right instead of pulling the eye along the diagonal.

Declared lighting is 'even ink-flat, no cast shadow gradient', yet the render shows a soft blurred photographic contact shadow under the strap (visible in contact_detail_crop as a gradient smudge). In a flat opaque-ink silkscreen concept this photographic smudge is the one element that breaks the material story; it should become a crisp flat printed ellipse footprint (or the bar alone should carry grounding).

References R1/R3 pair a dominant display headline and a structured secondary information layer with the hero; this poster has only three short lines top-left and an empty price slot at (104,1280), so the lower third right of the cobalt bar is unused cream. The piece stops at a competent generic constructivist pastiche rather than a resolved exhibition placard with a completed information hierarchy.
